question: A user edits a Google Doc directly in Drive after Claude referenced it earlier in a conversation, then asks a follow-up question about the same document. What should the user expect?
options: A) The user must re-upload the document as a new file for changes to appear.
B) Claude uses a cached snapshot from the first access and misses the new edits entirely.
C) Claude's view of the document reflects the latest Drive version, since it auto-syncs.
D) Claude only sees updates when the document is re-shared through a new link.
correct_answers: C) Claude's view of the document reflects the latest Drive version, since it auto-syncs.
explanations: Incorrect. Re-uploading is unnecessary because the connector already reads the live document from Drive.
Incorrect. There is no static cached snapshot behavior; the connector reflects the current Drive version instead.
Correct. Documents accessed through the Drive connector sync automatically with their Drive versions, so the follow-up reflects the latest edits.
Incorrect. Generating a new share link is not required, since syncing happens automatically for the existing reference.
